subject: Post-call summary: spend levers, expected ROI, and procurement timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@archpay.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@archpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary: spend levers, expected ROI, and procurement timeline

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps and assumptions for the pilot: 

Key pain points you called out:
- High per-request cost for ML features (NLP classification + chat) that scales with user volume
- Bursty traffic (end-of-day settlement windows) causing spikes and degraded latency
- Procurement wants clear, line-item estimates to justify a 90-day pilot before a 12-month commit

Goals for the pilot:
- Validate 95th percentile latency < 300ms for chat flows in the US region
- Demonstrate cost savings levers that lower per-100k-token unit cost by 20%+ vs current baseline
- Produce an ops checklist (runbook) for burst handling and failover to cheaper model variants

Cost/TCO assumptions we discussed (high-level):
- Baseline: ~ $160 per 1M input+output tokens on your current stack (what you reported)
- Redwood hosted baseline (unbatched): ~$110 per 1M tokens (estimate)
- Fast wins: batching + prefix/KV cache expected to reduce per-token by ~25–35% on your access pattern (we saw many repeated prefixes in your logs)
- Aggressive path: combining batching, 8-bit quantization model variant, and regional routing could reach ~40–45% savings for non-latency-critical requests

Suggested pilot scope & budget anchors (for procurement):
- 90-day pilot (dev+staging+production traffic slice)
- Monthly not-to-exceed: $30k (pilot cap) — we can shape configuration to stay within this by pinning model variant and enabling a cache policy
- Deliverables: latency report, per-route token economics, batching config recommendations, and a short ops runbook

Attachments: I attached a one-page SOW and a small model of batching savings that shows three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Please review.

Asks / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the pilot budget cap procurement is willing to approve (Tom / procurement)?
2) Provide a small sample of anonymized production traces (1–2M tokens) we can run in our evaluation harness — we only need prefixes and counts, not PII
3) Who should we coordinate with on the DPA / security questionnaire (email for legal/compliance)?

I'll open a shared folder with the pilot artifacts and a short onboarding checklist once you confirm the budget cap.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call summary: spend levers, expected ROI, and procurement timeline

Jonas — thanks, this is super helpful and aligns with what we heard internally. A few quick notes: 

- Procurement can greenlight a $30k/month pilot cap but wants the SOW to include a hard stop and a single-point contact for billing questions (that's Tom).
- Security: our InfoSec lead is Rebecca Shaw (rebecca.shaw@archpay.com). She'll want the SOC2 evidence and an initial answers-to-security-questions PDF.
- For the sample traces: we can provide a 1.2M-token anonymized dump by EOD Monday, 11 Aug. I'll work with our engineering ops to scrub PII.

One ask from our side: can you show a micro-simulation of how batching affects latency vs cost on the sample traces? If you can provide a short table (3 scenarios) in the batching_savings_model.xlsx that maps to % of requests batched, mean latency, and per-1M token cost, that will help Tom and procurement sign off faster.

If that works, we'll aim to circulate the signed minimal SOW next week.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Turner
Head of Product, ArchPay
lisa.turner@archpay.com

Great — appreciate the fast turnaround, Lisa. We'll add the hard stop to the SOW and put Tom as billing contact.

Planned deliverables for the micro-simulation (we'll drop into batching_savings_model.xlsx):
- Conservative: 10% batchable requests (baseline caching) — expected savings ~12%, mean latency delta +10ms
- Expected: 30% batchable requests (improved routing + prefix caching) — expected savings ~28%, mean latency delta +20ms
- Aggressive: 55% batchable requests (workload shaping + KV cache) — expected savings ~42%, mean latency delta +45ms

Note on latency: those latency deltas are for the batched path only; critical chat flows will remain pinned to the low-latency config (no batching) so we preserve the 95p SLO. The pilot can include a routing policy that splits traffic by route id so you can measure both sides.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Marissa will produce the updated SOW with a hard stop and billing contact (Tom).
- Ben will run the micro-simulation on the sample traces when you share them and return the populated spreadsheet.
- I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for next Wednesday to align on onboarding and monitoring.

I'll attach the updated SOW in the kickoff calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jonas
